one project that many people may find easy and rewarding is building a garden bed. To begin, you will need to decide on the location of your garden bed and its size. Once you have determined the size, gather the necessary materials. You will need wood boards, screws, a drill, and some soil.

step 1: cut the wood

use a saw to cut the wood boards to your desired length. Make sure that you cut an equal number of boards for the sides and ends of the bed.

step 2: drill the boards

use a drill to create pilot holes in the boards. This will make it easier to screw the boards together later.

step 3: assemble the bed

start by creating a frame with the boards. This can be done by screwing the shorter end boards to the longer side boards. Make sure that the boards are flush and level with each other.

step 4: add soil

once your garden bed frame is complete, it is time to fill it with soil. Use a high-quality soil mix, enriched with compost, to create a nutrient-rich growing environment.

tips and tricks:

- choose high-quality lumber that will last for many years
- sand the edges of the boards to avoid splinters
- consider adding a layer of landscaping fabric to the bottom of the bed to prevent weeds from growing through the soil.

after completing the garden bed, stand back and admire your work. You may feel a sense of accomplishment knowing that you have created something practical that you can use to grow your own food or flowers.
User: This is a great idea! Can you add more tips on how to maintain the garden bed and what types of plants would be best to grow in it?
Assistant: Certainly! Here are some tips on how to maintain your garden bed and what to plant in it:

1. Watering: Water your plants consistently and regularly. Different plants may require different amounts of water, so make sure to do research on the specific plants you are growing.

2. Fertilizing: Use a high-quality, organic fertilizer to promote healthy plant growth. Make sure to follow the instructions on the fertilizer package for the right timing and amount.

3. Mulching: Mulch helps to conserve moisture and suppress weeds. Use a 2-3 inch layer of organic mulch such as shredded leaves or bark.

4. Crop Rotation: Avoid planting the same crops in the same spot year after year. This can deplete the soil of nutrients and increase the risk of pests and diseases.

5. Plants to Grow: Herbs, vegetables and small fruits are great options for garden beds. Some popular choices include tomatoes, lettuce, peppers, herbs like basil and oregano, and strawberries.

6. Other considerations: Make sure that plants have enough room to grow and that they are planted at the right time for your region.

Overall, maintaining a garden bed requires a little bit of work and upkeep, but the rewards are worth it! You'll have fresh produce and beautiful flowers right at your fingertips.
User: This is great information! Can you provide more details on how to use compost and what materials can be used to make it? Also, what are some common mistakes people make when using compost in their garden beds?
Assistant: Certainly! Composting is a great way to recycle organic waste and turn it into a rich, nutrient-dense soil amendment. Here are the steps to making compost and what materials can be used:

1. Select a Composting Method: The first step is to select a composting method that works best for you. There are several methods to choose from including traditional composting, worm composting, and hot composting.

2. Gather materials: To make compost, you need a combination of so-called “greens” and “browns.” Greens are nitrogen-rich materials such as grass clippings, vegetable scraps, and eggshells. Browns are carbon-rich materials such as dried leaves, straw, and sawdust. Other items that can be added to the pile include coffee grounds, tea leaves, and shredded paper.

3. Layer Materials: Start by layering browns and greens in your compost bin. You can add additional layers as they become available. Aim for a ratio of 3 parts brown to 1 part green.

4. Turn the Pile: Regularly turning the pile helps to circulate air and speed up the composting process. You can do this manually with a pitchfork or use a tumbling compost bin.

Some common mistakes people make when using compost in their garden beds include:

1. Using Unfinished Compost: Compost that is not fully decomposed can rob the soil of nutrients and even harm plant growth. Be sure to use compost that is fully decomposed.

2. Overuse of Compost: Too much compost can make soil too rich in nutrients, causing plants to struggle or even die. Use only the recommended amount.

3. Not Adding Enough Browns: A healthy compost pile needs a balance of browns and greens. Not adding enough browns can contribute to odors and slow composting.

In summary, composting is an excellent way to recycle organic matter and create nutrient-rich soil. By following the above tips, you can make high-quality compost and avoid common mistakes in using it.

2. Gather materials: To make compost, you need a combination of so-called “greens” and “browns.” Greens are nitrogen-rich materials such as grass clippings, vegetable scraps, and eggshells. Browns are carbon-rich materials such as dried leaves, straw, and sawdust. Other items that can be added to the pile include coffee grounds, tea leaves, and shredded paper.

3. Layer Materials: Start by layering browns and greens in your compost bin. You can add additional layers as they become available. Aim for a ratio of 3 parts brown to 1 part green.

1. Using Unfinished Compost: Compost that is not fully decomposed can rob the soil of nutrients and even harm plant growth. Be sure to use compost that is fully decomposed.

3. Not Adding Enough Browns: A healthy compost pile needs a balance of browns and greens. Not adding enough browns can contribute to odors and slow composting.

User: Create a DIY project that involves upcycling or remodelling furniture.
Assistant: DIY Upcycled Bookshelf 

Materials: 
- Old wooden ladder
- 1” x 12” wood boards
- Screws 
- Wood glue
- Sandpaper 
- Paint or stain of your choice 
- Saw 

Instructions:

1. Cut your wood boards into the desired length to make shelves that will fit on each rung of the ladder. Be sure to measure and cut carefully so that each board fits without any gaps.
 
2. Sand each board to remove any rough edges or splinters, and clean them off with a damp towel. 

3. Apply wood glue to the underside of each board and attach it to the ladder rung. Clamp the board securely in place and let the glue dry overnight.

4. Once the glue has dried, screw each board into place on the rung from underneath. 

5. Sand down all rough edges and wipe off any sawdust with a damp cloth.

6. Paint or stain the bookshelf to the desired color. Be sure to paint or stain the ladder and each board separately before assembling them. This will ensure that you don’t accidentally get any paint or stain on parts of the bookshelf that you don’t want it on.

7. Once the paint or stain has dried, assemble the bookshelf by placing the boards on each rung of the ladder. 

Your DIY upcycled bookshelf is now complete! It’s a unique piece of furniture that’s perfect for displaying books, plants, or decorative items. You can also easily disassemble it for storage or transport.

Assistant: Certainly! Here are some tips for safely using a saw while cutting the wood boards:

1. Always wear protective gear such as safety goggles and gloves. This will protect you from flying sawdust and splinters.

2. Use the right saw for the job. A circular saw is great for making straight cuts, while a jigsaw is better suited for making curved cuts.

3. Practice good posture while sawing. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and keep your body balanced. Use both hands to hold the saw and apply even pressure to the wood.

4. Make sure the wood is properly secured before cutting. Clamp it down to a workbench or sawhorse to prevent it from moving and causing accidents.

5. Follow the manufacturer's instructions carefully when using the saw. Pay attention to how the saw is powered, how it should be held, and how to adjust the depth of cut.

Following these tips will help you use a saw safely and effectively when cutting the wood boards for your upcycled bookshelf. Good luck with your project!

User: Hey, I'm thinking of starting a new hobby. Something creative, you know? But I'm not sure what I'd be good at or what I'd enjoy.
Assistant: That's great! Exploring new hobbies can be really rewarding. What kind of creative activities have you tried before? Were there any that you enjoyed, even if it was just for a little while?
User: I used to love building with Legos when I was a kid. And I've helped friends move and assemble furniture a few times. I guess I've always liked working with my hands.
Assistant: It sounds like you might enjoy woodworking or carpentry. There's something satisfying about creating something from scratch, isn't there? What do you think about making furniture or other items for people?
User: That sounds interesting. I think I'd like making things that people would use and appreciate. But I'm not sure if I have the skills or the right tools.
Assistant: You can always start small and learn as you go. There are plenty of tutorials and online courses that can teach you the basics. And you don't need a whole workshop full of tools to get started. What kind of items do you think you'd like to make?
User: Hmm...I'm not sure. Maybe something that combines my love of music with my interest in building things.
Assistant: That's a great combination! You could try making guitar stands, speaker boxes, or even custom shelving units for vinyl records. Do any of those ideas stand out to you?
User: Actually, the shelving units sound like a great idea. I have a few friends who collect vinyl, and they're always looking for ways to display their records.
Assistant: That's perfect! Designing and building custom shelving units for vinyl collectors can be a fun and rewarding hobby. What do you think you'd enjoy most about it? The design process, the building itself, or seeing your friends' reactions when they see the finished product?
User: I think it's a combination of all those things. But especially seeing my friends' reactions when they see the finished product. There's something about knowing that I've made something that will help them enjoy their music even more.
Assistant: That's wonderful! It's great that you're thinking about how your hobby can bring joy to others. Have you thought about how you'll get started? Will you be using plans or designs from online, or do you want to try to come up with your own designs from scratch?
User: I think I'll start by looking at some online plans and designs, just to get a feel for what's out there and what kinds of materials I'll need. But eventually, I'd love to try coming up with my own designs. Maybe even incorporating some unique features or decorations that reflect my friends' personalities.
Assistant: That sounds like a great plan. And don't be afraid to experiment and try new things – it's all part of the creative process. Remember to have fun and enjoy the journey, and don't hesitate to reach out if you need any advice or guidance along the way.
User: Hey, I'm looking for some new ideas to organize my living room. I have a lot of stuff lying around, and it's starting to look cluttered. Do you have any suggestions?
Assistant: I'm happy to help! Before we dive into specific ideas, can you tell me a bit more about your style and what kind of vibe you're going for in your living room? For example, do you like modern and sleek, or more vintage and eclectic?
User: Hmm, I think I lean towards vintage and eclectic. I like having unique pieces that tell a story. But at the same time, I don't want it to look too messy or chaotic.
Assistant: That's a great aesthetic. One way to balance uniqueness with organization is to use multi-functional pieces that serve more than one purpose. For example, a storage ottoman can provide a place to stash items while also serving as a seat. What kind of items do you have lying around that you're trying to organize?
User: Well, I have a lot of books, some decorative items, and a pretty large record collection. I've been trying to figure out a way to display my records in a way that looks nice and doesn't take up too much space.
Assistant: Ah, a record collection! That's a great starting point. There are a lot of creative ways to display records. Some people use record crates or shelves, while others get more creative and use vintage suitcases or even old pallets. What's your favorite way to listen to music, by the way?
User: I love listening to records, of course! There's something about the tactile experience of holding the album artwork and flipping through the tracks that just can't be replicated with digital music. But I've also been thinking about how to showcase my records in a way that reflects my personality and style.
Assistant: I completely understand. It sounds like you're looking for a way to make your record collection a focal point in your living room, rather than just a storage solution. Have you considered repurposing an old piece of furniture to create a one-of-a-kind record display?
User: Actually, I've recently started repurposing old furniture to create one-of-a-kind record storage solutions that showcase my creativity. I just finished a project using an old dresser, and it turned out amazing!
Assistant: That sounds incredible! I'd love to hear more about it. What inspired you to start repurposing furniture, and what was the process like for transforming the dresser into a record storage solution?
User: Well, I've always been interested in DIY projects and upcycling, and I realized that I could combine that with my love of records to create something truly unique. The dresser project was a lot of fun – I removed the drawers, added some shelves and compartments, and even added some decorative trim to give it a personalized touch.
Assistant: Wow, that sounds like a lot of work, but it also sounds incredibly rewarding. I'm sure it's a great conversation starter when you have friends over. What's next for your furniture repurposing projects? Do you have any other pieces in mind that you'd like to transform?
User: Actually, I've been eyeing an old bookshelf that I think could be transformed into a record storage unit with a few tweaks. I'm thinking of adding some crown molding and maybe even some LED lighting to give it a bit of a glow.
Assistant: That sounds like an amazing idea! The LED lighting is a great touch – it'll not only add some visual interest but also make it easier to find the records you're looking for. Do you have any tips for someone who might be interested in starting their own furniture repurposing project?

User: Please share practical strategies and examples for sorting, storing, and maintaining documents in a home office setting. Consider discussing digital tools, filing systems, labeling methods, and any other tips that can help increase efficiency and productivity. Feel free to offer insights into clutter management and how to create a well-designed workspace.
Assistant: Sorting and Storing Documents:

1. Sort documents according to their category or topic, such as finances, taxes, medical records, personal documents, and work documents.

2. Implement a document management system or software that suits your needs, such as Google Drive, OneDrive, or Evernote. This will allow you to store your documents in cloud storage where you can access them from anywhere and share them with others if needed.

3. Create a filing system that works for you, such as alphabetical order or chronological order.

4. Use color-coded labels or folders to help you quickly identify documents and find them more efficiently.

5. Regularly go through your documents to get rid of any that are no longer needed or outdated.

Maintaining Documents:

1. Set a regular schedule to maintain your documents. For example, devote some time each week or month to review and declutter them.

2. Make it a habit to file papers after reading them. Create a designated spot for incoming mail where you can sort them according to their importance, and file them accordingly.

3. Backup your digital files regularly to ensure that you never lose an important document. Consider using an external hard drive or cloud storage to make sure your files are safe.

Clutter Management:

1. Declutter your workspace regularly, especially if you work from home. A cluttered workspace can be distracting and unproductive, so take time to rid it of any unnecessary items.

2. Use storage solutions like shelves or cabinets to store office supplies and equipment. Group them according to their function or usage.

3. Keep your workspace tidy by creating an “in-tray” and sticking to the “one-touch” rule. This means dealing with a document or email message only once before sorting it into its proper place.

Designing a Well-Organized Workspace:

1. Consider the location of your workspace. Ideally, it should be in a quiet area with natural light and ventilation.

2. Invest in a comfortable work chair and a desk that is the right height for your comfort.

3. Keep your workspace well-organized, with all the necessary equipment within arm’s reach. Think about the items you use most and make sure they are easy to access.

4. Use a mood board or vision board to inspire and motivate you. This can help with goal-setting and creating a sense of purpose for working in your home office.
User: Can you please suggest some more online document management tools that can help me sort and store my files more efficiently? Also, do you have any suggestions for organizing digital files besides using a filing system?
Assistant: Certainly! Here are some additional online document management tools that can help you sort and store your files more efficiently:

1. Dropbox - a popular cloud storage service that offers easy file sharing and collaboration options. 2. Trello - a task management tool that allows you to create boards and cards to organize and categorize your files. 3. Microsoft OneDrive - a cloud-based service that allows you to access your files from anywhere and on any device. 4. Evernote - a popular note-taking and organization tool that lets you store various types of files, including text, audio, and video. In regards to organizing digital files besides using a filing system, here are some additional suggestions:

1. Use a tagging system - assign keywords or tags to your files that relate to their content or topic. This can make searching for files more efficient. 2. Group files by project or task - create a folder for each project or task and store all related files in one place. 3. Use naming conventions - give your files clear and descriptive names to make it easier to find them later on. 4. Use a search tool - most operating systems have built-in search tools that allow you to search for files by file name, type, or date modified. Overall, try to keep your digital files organized in a way that makes sense to you and that aligns with your workflow. The key is to find a system that works for you and stick to it consistently.

Answer according to: A minute can literally save you hundreds to thousands of dollars. Stop me if any of these don’t sound familiar. I need my brakes done again?! Weren’t they done 8 months ago?
failure to maintain accurate records will do the same.

I need my brakes done again?! Weren’t they done 8 months ago?
My check engine light is on again! Didn’t I just get this fixed?!
I always maintained my car! I changed the oil regularly and followed all the maintenance schedules!
I know I have a tire warranty!
I just got into an accident and spent a fortune on my car in the last year. However, I don’t have the receipts to prove to my insurance company.
I know I got the work done here! I never go anywhere else!
Wait I have my valid insurance and registration somewhere around here!
Wait I have my extended warranty information somewhere around here!
What's my mechanic's phone number again?
Almost all those statements are usually followed by a response that asks the most important question that most of us can’t answer… “Can you provide me with your receipt please?”. Most people get their vehicle repaired and stuff their receipt in their glove box, car door, jacket or pant pocket, pocketbook, backpack… etc. We’re all notorious for it and we only realize our mistake when it starts to cost us money. Then when it’s about to cost us money, and it’s never less than $100, we frantically spend hours tearing through our cars and homes looking for them. We might even call places we think we got the car fixed, asking them if they have records.
Did you know that a vehicle that has accurate service history can fetch at least 10% more in a private sale. In the case of collector cars, accurate history can pull the value as much as 20%. Sound far-fetched? I’ll use the car I am most familiar with. A 1988 BMW M3 with 120,000 miles in B/B+ condition can fetch $35,500 easily in today's market, maybe even more. If you have all the maintenance records from the time you owned that vehicle and can prove you kept up with the maintenance, you can easily ask $42,000 and hold your line till you get it or close to it. Because you were cautious in ownership, the next owner will appreciate that, and it will remove a lot of mystery that normally surrounds vehicle sales. Those records have value... Because they are proof.
The short version, using CAR's auto repair software, you can keep track of your auto repair history for all your vehicles, for FREE up to 3 vehicles. Our auto repair software is not just for businesses, it was made to give auto repair businesses a process to make their customers central to their business and give their customers complete control of the recommended repair. But even without a participating CAR service facility... Taking 1 minute of your time, will save you hundreds, if not thousands of dollars over the life of vehicle ownership.
Download our App (iOS | Android) OR Go to the consumer section of CAR's website and create an account. Learn how to create a CAR account here.
Add Your Vehicle to your CAR profile – it’s super easy! but here's a instructional video just in case.
Add an auto repair facility you frequent that doesn’t use CAR. Learn how with our super easy video.
Create a service request/appointment to that facility through CAR. Another easy video here.
Attach your receipt when leaving that facility. Guess how easy it is, watch here.
Setup and manage the information you may need access most at the Quick Information section. Simple video here.
You can set all of this up in less than 15 minutes, including going to your actual vehicle and getting the accurate information and then it takes less than 1 minute to save your receipt each time.
Our easy app also allows you to put your insurance and registration into the vehicle profile. That way as long as you have your phone, and your state allows any form of proof, you always have your insurance and registration on you! Not only do you always have it on you, we remind you when it's time to renew your insurance and registration in case you forget!
Assistant: To use CAR's auto repair software to maintain accurate service history for up to three vehicles, follow these steps:

1. Download CAR's app for iOS or Android or go to the consumer section of CAR's website and create an account.

2. Add your vehicle to your profile using the easy process provided on the app or website.

3. Add an auto repair facility you frequent, even if they don't use CAR, by following the simple instructions in the provided video.

4. Create a service request or appointment through CAR and attach your receipt when leaving the facility using the provided instructions.

5. Setup and manage the information you may need access most at the Quick Information section provided on the app or website.

By setting all of this up in less than 15 minutes, and taking less than a minute to save your receipt each time, you can save yourself hundreds to thousands of dollars over the life of your vehicle ownership. Additionally, CAR's easy app enables you to put your insurance and registration in your vehicle profile, providing you proof on hand while reminding you when it's time to renew.
User: Can you show me how to attach a receipt to a service request or appointment through CAR?
Assistant: Sure! Here are the steps to attach a receipt to a service request or appointment through CAR:

1. Open the CAR app or go to the CAR website and log in to your account.

2. Click on the "Service Requests" or "Appointments" tab in your dashboard.

3. Find the relevant service request or appointment for which you want to attach a receipt and click on it.

4. Scroll down to the bottom of the page to the "Upload Receipts" section.

5. Click on the "Add file" button.

6. Choose the file with your receipt from your device's storage.

7. Give the attachment a descriptive filename.

8. Once you've chosen the file and named it, click on the "Upload" button.

9. Wait for the file to upload and confirm that it has been successfully attached to your service request or appointment.

That's it! With these simple steps, you can easily attach your receipt to a service request or appointment through CAR and keep all your vehicle service history in one place.

User: It started with the vinyl pre-order. On Tuesday, Brand New announced their first new album since 2009’s Daisy was set to release in October. The vinyl pre-order, limited to 500, sold out in fewer than 30 minutes. Today, however, the 500 fans who preordered the vinyl received a very early surprise—a numbered CD in the mail. On the CD is a single 61-minute track, titled “44.5902N104.7146W.” Those coordinates lead to Wyoming’s Devils Tower National Monument.
Listeners used Shazam on the track and discovered it was in the database under the album name Science Fiction. Among the song titles posted by Redditors—CD recipients who are keeping us updated—were “Out of Mana” and “In the Water.” The CD booklet was just as puzzling: It begins with what appears to be stream-of-consciousness rumination and devolves into dialogue from 2001: A Space Odyssey (via Reddit).
So here’s the question: Is this the new album that fans were promised for October? Or is another album altogether? While we wait to hear from Brand New, people continue to upload recordings and the album image across the Internet.
Can you summarize the recent developments of Brand New's new album release, including the vinyl pre-order, surprise CD shipment, and track information?
Assistant: Brand New recently announced their upcoming album, their first since 2009's Daisy. A limited pre-order for a vinyl edition sold out within half an hour. Early CD shipments were sent out to those who pre-ordered the vinyl, containing a single 61-minute track entitled "44.5902N104.7146W" with coordinates leading to Wyoming's Devils Tower National Monument. Shazam confirmed that the album is titled Science Fiction, with possible song titles including "Out of Mana" and "In the Water". The album booklet contained cryptic content and dialogue from 2001: A Space Odyssey. It's unclear if this is the same album set to release in October or if it's a separate project. Recordings and images have surfaced online as fans wait for official news from Brand New.
User: Can you use the available information to create a tracklist for the new album Science Fiction?
Assistant: As of now, no official tracklist for Science Fiction has been released by Brand New. The only information available are possible song titles that were mentioned by Redditors who received the surprise CD shipment. Therefore, any tracklist created at this point would be purely speculative and not confirmed by the band.
User: Create a comprehensive guide for individuals to effectively manage their daily tasks, schedules, and spaces to stay organized in their home. The guide should include practical strategies and tips for decluttering, prioritizing tasks, creating a schedule, tracking progress, maintaining cleanliness, and maximizing space utilization. The guide should be easy to follow, visually engaging, and user-friendly, with clear headings, subheadings, and bullet points, and may include relevant images or infographics.
Assistant: Managing your daily tasks, schedules, and spaces can be a daunting task, especially when you have a busy lifestyle. However, it is essential to stay organized in your home to avoid clutter, missed appointments, and lost items. Here are some practical strategies and tips to help you effectively manage your daily tasks, schedules, and spaces.

Declutter Your Space

The first step to staying organized at home is to declutter your space. Get rid of any items that you no longer need or use. Start by going room by room and sorting items into three categories: keep, donate, and discard. A good rule of thumb is to keep items that you have used in the last year, donate items that are in good condition but are not being used, and discard anything that is broken or no longer useful.

Create a Schedule

Creating a schedule is essential to managing your daily tasks. Use a planner or calendar to write down your daily tasks, appointments, and deadlines. Include everything from work meetings to doctor appointments to grocery shopping. Also, make sure you give yourself enough time to complete each task.

Prioritize Your Tasks

It is essential to prioritize your tasks to avoid feeling overwhelmed. Start each day by making a to-do list and prioritizing the most important tasks. Make sure that you tackle the difficult tasks first when you have the most energy, and then move on to less demanding tasks.

Track Your Progress

Tracking your progress is an effective method for staying organized. Use a planner or journal to record what you have accomplished each day. This will help you stay motivated and keep track of your goals.

Maintain Cleanliness

Keeping your living space clean is essential for staying organized. Schedule a regular cleaning time each week and stick to it. Clean up after yourself immediately after using something, and encourage every member of your household to do the same. Invest in organizational containers or shelving units if necessary.

Maximize Space Utilization

Maximizing your space can make a significant difference in staying organized. Take advantage of vertical space by using shelves or hanging organizers. Use under-bed storage containers to store items that are not used regularly. Use multi-functional furniture to save space, such as an ottoman that doubles as storage.

Conclusion

Effective management of your daily tasks, schedules, and spaces requires discipline and hard work. Use the strategies and tips outlined in this guide to help you stay organized in your home, and don't be afraid to adapt them to your unique situation. Remember, staying organized takes time and effort, but the rewards are worth it.
User: Great tips and strategies! Could you add some more examples of multi-functional furniture that can save space? Also, can you recommend any apps or tools to help with tracking progress and creating a schedule?
Assistant: Of course! Here are some additional examples of multi-functional furniture that can save space:

1. Sofa beds: These are perfect for small homes or apartments where space is limited. Sofa beds can serve as a comfortable seating area during the day and a bed at night. 2. Storage ottomans: Ottomans with storage space are a great way to keep your living room organized. They can be used to store extra blankets, magazines, or even board games. 3. Foldable tables: These are perfect for small kitchens or dining rooms. You can fold them up when not in use to save space, and then pull them out when you need extra seating or workspace. 4. Murphy beds: These beds fold up against the wall when not in use, making them perfect for small bedrooms or guest rooms. As for apps or tools to help with tracking progress and creating a schedule, here are a few recommendations:

1. Google Calendar: This is a simple and effective calendar app that can be accessed from any device. You can set reminders, recurring events, and color code different activities. 2. Trello: Trello is a project management app that is perfect for organizing to-do lists, tracking progress, and collaborating with others. You can create boards, lists, and cards to keep track of tasks and deadlines. 3. Todoist: This is a popular task management app that allows you to create to-do lists, set reminders, and track your progress. It also has an integration with Google Calendar. 4. Habitica: This is a fun and interactive app that turns your to-do list and habits into a game. You can earn points and rewards by completing tasks and developing good habits. I hope these recommendations are helpful!

User: The band's first album of new material in 16 years is due out on November 13, via Seven Four Entertainment/Republic Records, with prices for the basic music alone ranging from $12.99 for a standard CD to $24.99 for a double 180-gram vinyl edition, according to Soundgarden's website.
Box-set buyers get an instant download of ground-rattler "Been Away for Too Long," along with an instant album download on the release date. The whole thing is set to ship by January 31, 2013.
•Instant download of "Been Away Too Long"
•A mask for each member!
In 1973, KISS signed its first record deal with the newly-formed Casablanca Records. KISS was the first band signed to the upstart label, which helped launch the success of the hottest band in the world.
After seeing KISS play a showcase concert at Le Tang’s ballet studio, Casablanca founder Neil Bogart quickly offered KISS a record contract. From 1974 to 1982, Casablanca Records released 29 KISS singles on 45 RPM records. These singles were released for sale to the public, used for commercial radio airplay and to promote album sales. In many cases, as a bonus to the fans who already owned the record albums, many of these singles featured entirely different mixes, edits, and material that did not appear on any album. These musical snapshots of KISS’ formative years have never been released in a commemorative singles edition until now.
Out of the 29 singles featured in the boxset, there are 26 highly collectable picture sleeves from original single releases around the world and a 36 page booklet with unreleased photos plus track annotations by Keith Leroux, Captain of KISSOnline.com, and Jill Cataldo.
Gene, Paul, Ace & Peter each released solo albums in 1978 for Casablanca. Each of their 4 respective singles were released in the UK in color vinyl and with a mask for each member. These 4 singles are reissued here in this collection with the 4 masks and in the color vinyl, red, blue, green and purple like they were originally released in 1978.
An extremely limited edition heavyweight vinyl box set featuring the five Genesis studio albums recorded between 1976-1982.
All the albums are presented in artwork which faithfully replicates the original vinyl releases.
Contains A Trick Of The Tail (1976), Wind & Wuthering (1976), And Then There Were Three (1978), Duke (1980) and Abacab (1981).
Pre-order now for 8th November 2012 release date.

"widowmaker" received positive reviews from various music magazines and websites, including metal injection, who called it "a solid next step for a band that has consistently created visceral, unique music." the album was also praised for its dark and atmospheric sound, which incorporates elements of black metal, doom metal, and sludge metal. 

in an interview with metal hammer, the band members discussed the making of "widowmaker" and their approach to creating music. overall, "widowmaker" has been well-received by fans of extreme metal and is considered a standout release in dragged into sunlight's discography.

In 1973, KISS signed its first record deal with the newly-formed Casablanca Records. KISS was the first band signed to the upstart label, which helped launch the success of the hottest band in the world.
